title: Researching History Data

children:
Anytime something is impacted by either a system or user operation, the system 
 writes a history record identifying what happened. For example, when a 
 user picks an item from a location, the system generates a transaction 
 history record. This record identifies the user who picked the item, the 
 item and quantity picked, the location that it was removed from, the time/date 
 that the transaction occurred, and other pertinent information.
You can view system and user activity on several history insight screens: Transaction, Process, Quality, and            Receipt Quality.
Using the Receipt Quality History Insight Screen

The search fields displayed on a history insight screen will depend on which 
 type of history you are searching for. The following fields are especially 
 important in history searches. Use the help's index to access information 
 on other criteria fields.

Transaction Type: Indicates 
 the system transaction used on a particular piece of inventory.

Action:Indicates the actual work done in a process, such as the starting 
 of a build wave, or the cancelling of a wave.

Identifier 1-4:Each Identifier Field indicates part of the "history message 
 field," which the system generates with each process. Each field's 
 value will depend on the type of process you are researching.

Message:Indicates the message ID provides a descriptive explanation of 
 what happened during a process or action. The messages do not just identify 
 problems: they also identify any system action.

Process: Indicates an action 
 or decision that the system has performed.

Reason Code: Identifies why 
 an employee did not complete an outbound action as anticipated, such as 
 a pick (i.e. short picking a work instruction).

Vendor: Identifies the entity 
 that delivers product to your warehouse.

Reason Code: Identifies why 
 an employee did not complete an inbound action as anticipated, such as 
 checking in less than the original total quantity for the receipt 
 line.
